## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

1	# sheepdog — the fleet enforcer marker
2	
3	Declaring this pack marks a repo as the **fleet enforcer**: the one repo that covers and maintains
4	every repo under an owner. What the pack *is* — its six sweeps, their schedule, their reports, the
5	config schema — is [README.md](README.md). This file is what a session **here** has to get right.
6	
7	## Configuring the fleet
8	
9	- **Keeping a repo out of the fleet** — add its full `owner/name` to `exclude` on this pack's
10	  config entry. Nothing else opts a repo out: an archived or forked repo is reported as out of scope
11	  but still walked, and a repo that simply never adopted is `uncovered`, which is a finding rather
12	  than a choice. If a repo should not be measured, say so in `exclude` and the reports stop asking
13	  about it.
14	
15	- **Adding or changing a `packSeeds` entry** — get it right *before* the sweep next runs. The
16	  sweep seeds and never overrides, so a wrong seed reaches each member exactly once and then sticks;
17	  correcting it here un-writes nothing, and undoing it is a change in every member's repo. Land the
18	  entry and its own declaration together, then read the next run's report rather than assuming.
19	
20	- **Declaring a pack this fleet also seeds** — write the same config in both places, spelling
21	  every default out on both sides rather than leaving one implicit. `seeds-agree` compares them
22	  literally, because nothing in this pack may know what one pack's absent key means. A pack the
23	  fleet standardizes on but this repo does not itself run has nothing to agree with, and is fine.
24	
25	## Acting on what a sweep reports
26	
27	- **Acting on an `add-packs` work-list issue** — the work is a declaration and a reviewed PR **in
28	  the named member**, never here. A session in this repo is scoped to this repo, so if every item
29	  names another repo there is nothing here to do: say the scope is the blocker rather than writing
30	  to the issues, which are the only thing within reach and are not the work.
31	
32	- **Acting on a scanned pack suggestion** — it is a recommendation, never a verdict.
33	  A fingerprint is a way to *suspect* a pack is wanted; whether to declare it is the member's call,
34	  and closing the issue `not planned` is a standing answer the scan honours rather than re-opening.
35	  A **forced** addition is the other thing entirely — a decision already made — so adopt what
36	  its issue says instead of re-judging whether it was wanted.
37	
38	- **Reading `unknown` in a report** — it means the sweep could not look, not that it looked and
39	  found nothing. Never convert one into a verdict: a repo whose declaration could not be read is
40	  neither covered nor uncovered, an undecided fingerprint is not a non-match, and a member the
41	  pack-seed sweep could not reach is not converged. Fix the access and re-run.
42	
43	- **Judging whether a member is behind** — compare `engineVersion` and `packVersions` against
44	  canon, never the age of its stamped `ref`. The update flows deliberately never rewrite `ref` or
45	  `updated`, so on a well-maintained member the stamp is frozen and its age measures nothing.
46	  The stamped `ref` is provenance: it says which commit first vendored the mount, and stays
47	  frozen on a member that is perfectly current.
48	
49	- **Answering why the fleet did not move** — read the member's own artifacts first: its
50	  declaration, its stamp, the runs on its head sha. This repo dispatches; each member converges
51	  itself, with its own token and its own delivery policy. Propose a settings change as a conclusion,
52	  never as the diagnosis.
53	
54	## Running the manual levers
55	
56	- **Pushing canon to the whole fleet now** — create the work item, from a checkout of this repo:
57	
58	  ```
59	  node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/create-work-item.mjs sheepdog/fleet-baseline
60	  ```
61	
62	  Add `--context "REPOS=owner/a owner/b"` to narrow it (space-separated: a Context line splits on
63	  commas), `--context "DRY_RUN=true"` to see the list without dispatching, or
64	  `--context "INCLUDE_DORMANT=true"` to reach members that stopped their own scheduler on purpose.
65	  Both knobs are read from the item's Context and nowhere else — an item created without them runs
66	  unscoped and live. It queues one
67	  run per member and does not wait; each member reports its own outcome in its own repo. A member
68	  with nothing to do converges to a cheap no-op, so over-using it is wasteful rather than unsafe.
69	
70	- **Catching the digest up after an outage** — the same lever, with the day count:
71	
72	  ```
73	  node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/create-work-item.mjs sheepdog/fleet-digest \
74	    --context "DIGEST_BACKFILL_DAYS=7"
75	  ```
76	
77	  It covers the N most recent complete UTC days, oldest first, skips any day that already has a
78	  brief, and is bounded at 30 days a run — so it is safe to re-run and safe to overlap with the
79	  daily task.
80	
81	- **Adding a pack across the fleet** — create a `fleet-add-missing-packs` item with
82	  `--context "ADD_PACKS=…"` rather than editing anything. No pack is named anywhere in this pack's
83	  code: every id comes from config or from the item's own Context, which is what keeps the
84	  enforcer from becoming a second place packs are known.
85	
86	## Credentials
87	
88	- **Granting or repairing `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`** — a fine-grained PAT spanning the owner's
89	  repositories, with Metadata read, **Contents read and write**, Issues read/write, Pull requests
90	  read, and **Actions read and write**. Contents write is the pack-seed sweep writing one
91	  declaration into each member; Actions write is the two fan-out tasks dispatching another member's
92	  workflow.
93	
94	- **A fan-out task reporting `no-permission`** — the PAT is missing Actions:
95	  read and write, and every member answers `403`. It is a grant to fix once, so widen the token
96	  rather than re-running: neither task retries, because a work list nobody will act on is not a
97	  green outcome.

16	It **reports; it does not repair** — `expected_outcome: none`. Adoption issues open while a repo is uncovered, close `completed` once covered and `not planned` once excluded. Drift issues open while a member is unhealthy, close `completed` once fresh again and `not planned` once the repo leaves the fleet; an already-open one is re-commented only when its **root cause changes**, which is what lets this ride a daily cadence without turning every thread into a wall of identical notes.
17	
18	## Why one task
19	
20	These were two — a daily `fleet-census` and a weekly `fleet-freshness` — and each carried its own enumeration, its own owner filter, its own empty-enumeration guard, its own home/canon/archived/fork/excluded skips and its own declaration read per repo. The freshness half's header said it *"takes coverage as given"*, but it could not: the census's verdict lived in another process on another cadence, so it re-derived the whole thing.
21	
22	That produced divergence in the classification itself. `exclude` was applied at different points, so an excluded repo that still carried a declaration read **covered** to one sweep and **out of scope** to the other. And each half's `unknown` failed its own run knowing nothing of the other's, so one green run beside one red one told a reader nothing about which half of the fleet picture to trust.
23	
24	One walk means one membership verdict per repo, one report, and one failure boundary. See [#788](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/788).
25	
26	## The freshness classification
27	
28	For each measured member, by **root cause**, in this precedence:
29	
30	| state | meaning |
31	|---|---|
32	| `no-stamp` | declares packs but was never vendored — no engine on disk at all |
33	| `no-scheduler` | no vendored scheduler workflow, so no cron, so it will never baseline itself; every other symptom is downstream of this |
34	| `ref-not-on-trunk` | the stamped ref is not a canon commit, or not an ancestor of canon's default branch — vendoring's #328 anti-rewind guard refuses to write, so the repo is **wedged**, not merely late |
35	| `behind` | on trunk, but its stamped `engineVersion` is below canon's or a pack it stamps is below that pack's manifest version in canon — the self-refresh has stopped landing |
36	| `fresh` | every version it stamps is at canon's |
37	
38	### What `behind` measures, and what it deliberately does not
39	
40	The **version gap**, and nothing else. The versioned update flows stamp `engineVersion` and `packVersions` and never rewrite `ref` or `updated`, so on a well-maintained member the stamped ref is frozen at whatever commit first vendored the mount: it is provenance, and its **age** measures nothing. Worse, it does not decay gracefully — every member's ref ages at the same rate, so one arbitrary day the whole fleet crosses any date window at once and the sweep files a drift issue per repo for a fleet that is, by versions, current ([#1025](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1025)).
41	
42	The numbers are read out of **canon** over the API — `engine/version.mjs` and each `packs/<id>/pack.mjs` — never out of the enforcer's own mount, which is itself a member and can be behind. A pack canon no longer carries has no manifest to be behind and is skipped; an absent number never reads as zero. A stamp carrying neither number is behind by construction: an engine that stamps always stamps.
43	
44	The stamped ref is still read, for the one thing it honestly says — whether it is a commit on canon's trunk at all, which is the `ref-not-on-trunk` wedge.
45	
46	## Who is measured by which question
47	
48	Every repo lands in exactly one bucket per question, and the two disagree on purpose:
49	
50	- **The enforcer** is censused by neither — it is named in both summaries and swept by its own scheduler.
51	- **Canon** is an ordinary covered member to the coverage question (it carries a declaration) and is never measured by the freshness one (it has no vendored mount to be stale).
52	- **An excluded repo** that still carries a declaration is **covered** — saying otherwise would report a repo as missing something it has — and is **out of scope** for freshness, because upkeep is what the exclusion opted out of.
53	- **A dormant member** (`"dormant": true`, [the scheduler's gate](../../../core/scheduled-tasks.md)) is a covered member with no freshness verdict: its stamp is never read, and any open drift issue for it closes *not planned*. Its scheduler is stopped, so its mount falls behind **by design**. The test is `isDormant`, re-exported from the engine rather than re-implemented — a sweep with a private notion of dormancy would nag exactly the repos that had already opted out.
54	
55	## Why daily, and what it costs
56	
57	The freshness question was weekly because drift is measured in days and a daily re-ask could not change its answer. Merged, that argument buys nothing: the walk runs daily for the coverage question regardless, and gating half the task on a cadence it computed itself would reimplement dueness — which the engine owns (the tick instantiates a task's item when its anchor comes) and is not something a task can ask about from inside itself.
58	
59	So the freshness probe runs daily too, at roughly **two extra REST reads per covered member** on the six days that used to be coverage-only. **This merge is not an API-call saving and is not claimed as one.** What it buys is one roster instead of two that can disagree; drift converging within a day rather than a week is the side benefit.
60	
61	## Not a fleet mechanism
62	
63	Its *implementation* scans every repo under the owner, but its declaration, scheduling and lifecycle are those of **any pack task**: it is active because this repo declares the `sheepdog` pack, and it runs on this repo's ordinary scheduler. It declares no `fleet` signal and no `fleet` session scope — the cross-repo reach lives in the implementation, never in the wiring.
64	
65	## Failure is loud, and now per-question
66	
67	A repo whose **declaration** cannot be read or parsed is `unknown` to **both** questions — it is the input they share. A repo whose **mount probe** fails (the stamp read, canon's compare) is `unknown` to the **freshness** question alone: the coverage question already read that declaration successfully and keeps its verdict.
68	
69	Either kind fails the run: no issue is opened for an unknown repo, no open issue is closed on its behalf, and the sweep exits non-zero with both halves' unknowns named together. The executor treats a non-zero prework subprocess as a failed task and converges the item to `needs-human`, so an unusable token or scope escalates rather than silently shrinking the fleet.

input.body:
Fixes #1025.

## The bug

`fleet-roster`'s `behind` state measured the **age of the stamped ref**. The versioned update flows deliberately never rewrite `ref`, so every member's stamp is frozen at whatever commit first vendored it — and every member's ref ages at the same rate. With the fleet stamped at `631a067` (2026-08-13) and `staleDays: 14`, the condition would have gone true for **every member at once on 2026-08-27**, opening a `fleet-drift` issue per repo for a fleet that is, by versions, current.

## What `behind` measures now

The **version gap**, and nothing else:

- stamped `engineVersion` below canon's `ENGINE_VERSION`, or
- any stamped `packVersions` entry below that pack's manifest `version` in canon,

with the gap named in the drift issue (`behind canon by engine v3 → v4, basics v5 → v7`).

Both numbers are read out of **canon** over the API — `engine/version.mjs` and `packs/<id>/pack.mjs` — never out of the enforcer's own mount, which is itself a member and can be behind. The reader is memoized per sweep, so canon is read once per *distinct pack* across the whole walk rather than once per member.

Two shapes the classifier refuses to guess at: a pack canon has retired has no manifest to be behind and contributes no gap (an absent number never reads as zero), and a manifest that is present but whose version can't be parsed **throws**, which becomes `unknown` for that member and fails the run.

A stamp carrying neither number is `behind` by construction — an engine that stamps always stamps.

## What is unchanged

`no-stamp`, `no-scheduler` and `ref-not-on-trunk` all read the ref for what it still honestly is, provenance. The compare call stays for the `ref-not-on-trunk` wedge (#328); only its `ahead_by` and base-commit date are no longer read.

The body marker still spells `fleet-freshness` and the `behind` state token is unchanged, so open drift issues are read rather than re-opened as `unrecorded`.

## `staleDays`

With no date measure left it governs nothing, so it is retired from `parseSheepdogConfig`, from the report header, from the drift issue body and from the docs. An enforcer config still carrying the key is read, not rejected — unknown keys were always ignored.

## Also

- `packs/sheepdog/pack.mjs` version 6 → 7 (delivery signal).
- `task.md`'s "the one assumption" section rewritten; its pointer to the closed #786 removed.
- `RULES.md`'s "judging whether a member is behind" bullet no longer claims `staleDays` governs a legacy measure.

## Verification

- New tests written first and watched fail (the module had no `canonVersions` export), then green.
- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`: 2099 pass, 1 fail — `engine-pack-lane-shims`, which fails identically on a stashed tree ("this checkout is too shallow to walk origin/main's pack history").
- `check_the_work`: clean. `check_the_world`: 0 blocking, and the one advisory this change introduced (`task-phase-discipline`) was removed by rewording rather than waived.

{"number":1028,"title":"sheepdog: judge fleet freshness by stamped versions, not ref age","body":"Fixes #1025.

## The bug

`fleet-roster`'s `behind` state measured the **age of the stamped ref**. The versioned update flows deliberately never rewrite `ref`, so every member's stamp is frozen at whatever commit first vendored it — and every member's ref ages at the same rate. With the fleet stamped at `631a067` (2026-08-13) and `staleDays: 14`, the condition would have gone true for **every member at once on 2026-08-27**, opening a `fleet-drift` issue per repo for a fleet that is, by versions, current.

## What `behind` measures now

The **version gap**, and nothing else:

- stamped `engineVersion` below canon's `ENGINE_VERSION`, or
- any stamped `packVersions` entry below that pack's manifest `version` in canon,

with the gap named in the drift issue (`behind canon by engine v3 → v4, basics v5 → v7`).

Both numbers are read out of **canon** over the API — `engine/version.mjs` and `packs//pack.mjs` — never out of the enforcer's own mount, which is itself a member and can be behind. The reader is memoized per sweep, so canon is read once per *distinct pack* across the whole walk rather than once per member.

Two shapes the classifier refuses to guess at: a pack canon has retired has no manifest to be behind and contributes no gap (an absent number never reads as zero), and a manifest that is present but whose version can't be parsed **throws**, which becomes `unknown` for that member and fails the run.

A stamp carrying neither number is `behind` by construction — an engine that stamps always stamps.

## What is unchanged

`no-stamp`, `no-scheduler` and `ref-not-on-trunk` all read the ref for what it still honestly is, provenance. The compare call stays for the `ref-not-on-trunk` wedge (#328); only its `ahead_by` and base-commit date are no longer read.

The body marker still spells `fleet-freshness` and the `behind` state token is unchanged, so open drift issues are read rather than re-opened as `unrecorded`.

## `staleDays`

With no date measure left it governs nothing, so it is retired from `parseSheepdogConfig`, from the report header, from the drift issue body and from the docs. An enforcer config still carrying the key is read, not rejected — unknown keys were always ignored.

## Also

- `packs/sheepdog/pack.mjs` version 6 → 7 (delivery signal).
- `task.md`'s "the one assumption" section rewritten; its pointer to the closed #786 removed.
- `RULES.md`'s "judging whether a member is behind" bullet no longer claims `staleDays` governs a legacy measure.

## Verification

- New tests written first and watched fail (the module had no `canonVersions` export), then green.
- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`: 2099 pass, 1 fail — `engine-pack-lane-shims`, which fails identically on a stashed tree ("this checkout is too shallow to walk origin/main's pack history").
- `check_the_work`: clean. `check_the_world`: 0 blocking, and the one advisory this change introduced (`task-phase-discipline`) was removed by rewording rather than waived.

{"number":1028,"title":"sheepdog: judge fleet freshness by stamped versions, not ref age","body":"Fixes #1025.

## The bug

`fleet-roster`'s `behind` state measured the **age of the stamped ref**. The versioned update flows deliberately never rewrite `ref`, so every member's stamp is frozen at whatever commit first vendored it — and every member's ref ages at the same rate. With the fleet stamped at `631a067` (2026-08-13) and `staleDays: 14`, the condition would have gone true for **every member at once on 2026-08-27**, opening a `fleet-drift` issue per repo for a fleet that is, by versions, current.

## What `behind` measures now

The **version gap**, and nothing else:

- stamped `engineVersion` below canon's `ENGINE_VERSION`, or
- any stamped `packVersions` entry below that pack's manifest `version` in canon,

with the gap named in the drift issue (`behind canon by engine v3 → v4, basics v5 → v7`).

Both numbers are read out of **canon** over the API — `engine/version.mjs` and `packs//pack.mjs` — never out of the enforcer's own mount, which is itself a member and can be behind. The reader is memoized per sweep, so canon is read once per *distinct pack* across the whole walk rather than once per member.

Two shapes the classifier refuses to guess at: a pack canon has retired has no manifest to be behind and contributes no gap (an absent number never reads as zero), and a manifest that is present but whose version can't be parsed **throws**, which becomes `unknown` for that member and fails the run.

A stamp carrying neither number is `behind` by construction — an engine that stamps always stamps.

## What is unchanged

`no-stamp`, `no-scheduler` and `ref-not-on-trunk` all read the ref for what it still honestly is, provenance. The compare call stays for the `ref-not-on-trunk` wedge (#328); only its `ahead_by` and base-commit date are no longer read.

The body marker still spells `fleet-freshness` and the `behind` state token is unchanged, so open drift issues are read rather than re-opened as `unrecorded`.

## `staleDays`

With no date measure left it governs nothing, so it is retired from `parseSheepdogConfig`, from the report header, from the drift issue body and from the docs. An enforcer config still carrying the key is read, not rejected — unknown keys were always ignored.

- `packs/sheepdog/pack.mjs` version 6 → 7 (delivery signal).
- `task.md`'s "the one assumption" section rewritten; its pointer to the closed #786 removed.
- `RULES.md`'s "judging whether a member is behind" bullet no longer claims `staleDays` governs a legacy measure.

{"number":1028,"title":"sheepdog: judge fleet freshness by stamped versions, not ref age","body":"Fixes #1025.

## The bug

`fleet-roster`'s `behind` state measured the **age of the stamped ref**. The versioned update flows deliberately never rewrite `ref`, so every member's stamp is frozen at whatever commit first vendored it — and every member's ref ages at the same rate. With the fleet stamped at `631a067` (2026-08-13) and `staleDays: 14`, the condition would have gone true for **every member at once on 2026-08-27**, opening a `fleet-drift` issue per repo for a fleet that is, by versions, current.

## What `behind` measures now

The **version gap**, and nothing else:

- stamped `engineVersion` below canon's `ENGINE_VERSION`, or
- any stamped `packVersions` entry below that pack's manifest `version` in canon,

with the gap named in the drift issue (`behind canon by engine v3 → v4, basics v5 → v7`).

Both numbers are read out of **canon** over the API — `engine/version.mjs` and each pack's `pack.mjs` — never out of the enforcer's own mount, which is itself a member and can be behind. The reader is memoized per sweep, so canon is read once per *distinct pack* across the whole walk rather than once per member.

Two shapes the classifier refuses to guess at: a pack canon has retired has no manifest to be behind and contributes no gap (an absent number never reads as zero), and a manifest that is present but whose version can't be parsed **throws**, which becomes `unknown` for that member and fails the run.

A stamp carrying neither number is `behind` by construction — an engine that stamps always stamps.

## What is unchanged

`no-stamp`, `no-scheduler` and `ref-not-on-trunk` all read the ref for what it still honestly is, provenance. The compare call stays for the `ref-not-on-trunk` wedge (#328); only its `ahead_by` and base-commit date are no longer read.

The body marker still spells `fleet-freshness` and the `behind` state token is unchanged, so open drift issues are read rather than re-opened as `unrecorded`.

## `staleDays`

With no date measure left it governs nothing, so it is retired from `parseSheepdogConfig`, from the report header, from the drift issue body and from the docs. An enforcer config still carrying the key is read, not rejected — unknown keys were always ignored.

## Also

- `packs/sheepdog/pack.mjs` version 7 → 8 (delivery signal).
- `task.md`'s "the one assumption" section rewritten; its pointer to the closed #786 removed.
- `RULES.md`'s "judging whether a member is behind" bullet no longer claims `staleDays` governs a legacy measure.

## Verification

- New tests written first and watched fail (the module had no `canonVersions` export), then green.
- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` on the rebased head: 2131 pass, 1 fail — `engine-pack-lane-shims`, which fails identically on a stashed tree ("this checkout is too shallow to walk origin/main's pack history").
- `check_the_work`: clean. `check_the_world`: 0 blocking, and the one advisory this change introduced (`task-phase-discipline`) was removed by rewording rather than waived.
- Rebased onto `cae5273` after #1013 landed; its `prework` → `code_work` rename conflicted with the `staleDays` removal on one README line, both sides kept.

description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.

The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.

## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)

Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later, in the conversation half of the repo's scheduled `growth-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.

## Don't

- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.
